summary: The bill expands ESOPs in S corporations by accelerating full tax deferral on sales of employer stock to such plans, letting ESOP-majority firms keep their small-business eligibility for SBA loans and preferences, and creating a Treasury technical-assistance office plus a Labor Department advocate for employee ownership.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes new federal offices (S Corporation Employee Ownership Assistance Office at Treasury and Advocate for Employee Ownership at Labor) and authorizes appropriations for the latter. These provisions create modest new administrative costs and expand the scope of government activity, though the overall fiscal impact is limited.

Sections 3(a) and 3(b) accelerate and expand tax deferral under IRC section 1042 for sales of employer stock to S corporation ESOPs by moving the effective date forward and repealing the prior limitation in subsection (h). This constitutes a targeted tax incentive that reduces tax liability for qualifying transactions.
